UNDERSTANDING BITUMEN PRICING
WHY BITUMEN PRICES MOVE — AND HOW BUYERS AVOID OVERPAYING

LAST REVIEWED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 · PETROBIND EXPORT DESK

A bitumen quotation is not one number pulled from a price sheet. It reflects crude cost, refinery output, packing, freight, and — often overlooked — how tight regional stock is at the moment of quoting. Buyers who understand these drivers can judge a quote against the market.

Request Bitumen Quote
View Bitumen Grades
WHAT ACTUALLY MOVES THE PRICE

Bitumen is a refinery by-product, so its price tracks crude oil cost and refinery run rates, but it also has its own supply-demand cycle. When regional refineries cut output or redirect capacity, available stock tightens even while crude prices stay flat.

Crude oil cost and refinery vacuum-distillation output.

Regional stock levels — tight stock alone can move price independent of crude.

Freight and bunker fuel cost between origin and destination port.

Packing format (drums, bulk, bitutainer) and seasonal shipping demand.

REGIONAL STOCK TIGHTNESS AND THE QUOTE

When supply is tight in a corridor, a quote can carry a premium that reflects a supplier's access to product rather than a change in the material itself. Buyers who understand the cost drivers — crude, refinery output, freight, and regional stock — are better placed to judge whether a quote is in line with the market.

HOW PETROBIND APPROACHES PRICING

PetroBind buys direct from the supplier, not through a broker chain, and works to keep a quote competitive on landed cost. Pricing is market-linked and quoted per RFQ against grade, quantity, destination, and Incoterm.
